contributions.statement: When judging a router or cascade, report the share of items within a tolerance of the strong-model reference, not only mean quality. A difficulty-only router raised mean quality but lowered parity below cheap-only, because the easy items it left unguarded regressed.
contributions.evidence: Appendix F.1, Table 2: naive difficulty router mean 4.543 > low-cost 4.400, but within-0.5 parity 72% < 78%; 9 queries drive it (5 easy, 3 medium, 1 hard). n=50, one sample, LLM judge.

contributions.statement: Cheap model drafts, a cheap rubric evaluator accepts, a critic rewrites borderline answers, and only failures escalate to the premium model.
contributions.evidence: §3.4, Algorithm 1, Table 2: 18% escalation vs 28% for a generic cascade, but quality margin over generic cascade CI [-0.040, +0.168].

reason: Self-declared WIP. The cascade is FrugalGPT-style, with an added rewrite band whose benefit over a plain cascade is not resolved. The mean-vs-parity observation is the only new angle, and it rests on 9 queries.
